ruleName: Restrictions on Touching Sand in Bunker
title: Accidentally Touching the Sand in a Bunker
question: Your ball is in a bunker. As you walk towards it, you accidentally lose your balance and your hand touches the sand beside your ball. What is the correct ruling?

choices.text: You receive the general penalty because you touched the sand in the bunker.
You receive a one-stroke penalty because you touched the sand before making a stroke.
There is no penalty because the contact with the sand was accidental and did not improve the conditions affecting your stroke.
You must rake the area before playing your shot.

explanation: The Rules no longer prohibit every contact with the sand in a bunker. There is no penalty if you accidentally touch the sand, such as keeping your balance, entering or leaving the bunker, or placing your clubs in the bunker, provided you do not improve the conditions affecting your stroke. Penalty only applies if you deliberately touch the sand to test its condition, or improve conditions affecting your stroke. Rule Reference: Rule 12.2b.
imagePrompt: A modern semi-realistic (75% realistic, 25% stylised) illustration in a clear, polished junior golf quiz style. Show a bunker on a golf course with a green in the background. A golfer is in the bunker, having just lost their balance, and their hand is on the sand near their ball. The ball is lying clearly on the bunker sand several feet from the player's hand. It must be obvious that the contact is accidental (such as through body posture suggesting recovering balance). The player’s club is not touching the sand. Golfer with one hand touching the sand near the ball in a way that clearly indicates loss of balance or an accidental touch
Player not holding a club against the sand
